raw_comment: I notice that me majority of the worst droughts are occurring in the middle of the U.S., far from the ocean; however, there is still notable scarcity of precipitation in places near the coasts too like in New Jersey, Delaware, and Washington. I wonder what changed behind the reasoning of the growing rates of droughts recently compared to events that caused droughts previously and didn't have as much of an impact. This relates to my community because while we are not experiencing extreme droughts, the areas north and south of us are experiencing this. It can alter the amount of food being produced by farmers in the U.S. increasing the prices of foods in the U.S. A catchy title would be "Drought Levels Across the United States."
